# package parts

`import "github.com/lestrrat-3d/decad/parts"`

[Module index](<README.md>)

<a name="pkg-overview"></a>
## Overview

Package parts is a generic schematic and exploded view of a build made of
separate bodies (agent-docs/parts-design.md). A [Set](<#Set>) names the placed bodies
of one document and the joints between them; Explode, [Graph](<#Graph>) and the other
queries read the [Set](<#Set>) and change neither it nor the document.

parts knows nothing of how a part is made.

<a name="WithWitnessSearch"></a>
#### func WithWitnessSearch

<pre>func WithWitnessSearch() <a href="#CheckOption">CheckOption</a></pre>

WithWitnessSearch makes Check also look for a witness for each unexplained
pair: a point whose distances to the two parts prove the pair within the
contact tolerance of each other, which Check then reports as [PairFinding](<#PairFinding>).Near.
A pair without Near may be apart. The search samples up to 128 mesh vertices
per pair and calls Body.DistanceToPoint at each.

<a name="WithDerivedExplode"></a>
#### func WithDerivedExplode

<pre>func WithDerivedExplode() <a href="#ExplodeOption">ExplodeOption</a></pre>

WithDerivedExplode derives the removal order and direction of every part that
no WithExplodeStages entry names from the parts' tessellations, instead of
walking the joints. Explicit stages run first, unchanged. A part leaves along a
joint axis, a stated pull or a world axis once no part still present stands in
its way; parts that block each other leave together as one rigid group. A pair
the tessellation cannot decide counts as free, so the result is a layout and
not a proof (agent\-docs/parts\-design.md §5.8).

#### func WithExplodeGap

<pre>func WithExplodeGap(gap units.Value) <a href="#ExplodeOption">ExplodeOption</a></pre>

WithExplodeGap sets how far past full disengagement each part moves; the
default is 10 mm. A zero gap is allowed.

<a name="WithExplodeScale"></a>
#### func WithExplodeScale

<pre>func WithExplodeScale(scale units.Value) <a href="#ExplodeOption">ExplodeOption</a></pre>

WithExplodeScale multiplies every final offset by scale, a positive
Dimensionless value: a uniform spread about the assembled layout. The default
is units.Scalar(1).

<a name="WithExplodeStages"></a>
#### func WithExplodeStages

<pre>func WithExplodeStages(stages ...<a href="#Stage">Stage</a>) <a href="#ExplodeOption">ExplodeOption</a></pre>

WithExplodeStages runs the explosion in the given stages, in order. A part no
stage names, other than the ground, forms a last stage named "" that clears its
joined neighbours by WithExplodeGap's gap. With no stages every part is in that
last stage.

<pre>func WithPartGap(part <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#string">string</a>, gap units.Value) <a href="#ExplodeOption">ExplodeOption</a></pre>

WithPartGap sets one part's gap, in place of its stage's and
WithExplodeGap's. A part no [Set](<#Set>) has is decad.ErrDegenerate at the query.

<a name="WithRemoval"></a>
#### func WithRemoval

<pre>func WithRemoval(part <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#string">string</a>, r <a href="#Removal">Removal</a>) <a href="#ExplodeOption">ExplodeOption</a></pre>

WithRemoval constrains the derived removal of one part and needs
WithDerivedExplode. A part no [Set](<#Set>) has, a part without a body, the ground,
or a part an explicit stage names is decad.ErrDegenerate at the query, as is a
constraint the search cannot meet. A later WithRemoval for the same part
replaces the earlier one.

<a name="Exploded.Hidden"></a>
#### func (\*Exploded) Hidden

<pre>func (e *<a href="#Exploded">Exploded</a>) Hidden(view r3.Vec) ([]<a href="#Occlusion">Occlusion</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

Hidden lists the pairs of exploded parts where one may hide the other seen along
view, which points from the camera into the scene: each part's box is projected
orthographically along view to a rectangle, and a pair whose rectangles overlap
is listed with the nearer part (the one whose box centre is nearer the camera)
as Front, and the share of Back's rectangle Front's covers. A pair absent from
the list cannot hide one another; a listed pair may, since a box is larger than
its part. Hidden moves nothing. A zero view is decad.ErrDegenerate and a
non-finite one decad.ErrNotFinite. Pairs come in Parts order.

<a name="Graph.WriteMermaid"></a>
#### func (Graph) WriteMermaid

<pre>func (g <a href="#Graph">Graph</a>) WriteMermaid(w io.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/io#Writer">Writer</a>) <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a></pre>

WriteMermaid writes a left-to-right Mermaid flowchart: one subgraph per
non-root group, a rectangle for a manufactured part and a rounded node for a
purchased one, and one edge per joint from A to B labelled with its kind, its
motion when not fixed, its status when known and, when the joint is not
Confirmed, its cause in brackets. A Contradicted edge ends in a cross (--x) and
an Undecided one is dotted; the others keep the plain arrow.

<a name="Joint"></a>
### type Joint

<pre>type Joint struct {
    Name   <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#string">string</a> // unique within the Set; empty names get &#34;A~B&#34;
    Kind   <a href="#JointKind">JointKind</a>
    A, B   <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#string">string</a> // part names
    Motion <a href="#Motion">Motion</a>
    // Axis is the author&#39;s statement of a PinInBore&#39;s or PinInSlot&#39;s axis, in
    // assembled world coordinates, or nil. The faces&#39; own axis is used when
    // they show one; Axis is the fallback where they do not, and Check reports
    // a declared axis the faces contradict.
    Axis *<a href="#Axis">Axis</a>
    // Clearance is the declared radial clearance of a PinInBore or the
    // declared side clearance of a PinInSlot, a signed Length: negative is a
    // press fit. The zero Value declares none, and Check reports the measured
    // clearance without judging it.
    Clearance units.Value
    // MinGap is a Keepout&#39;s least allowed gap, a Length &gt; 0.
    MinGap units.Value
    // Direction is a Slides joint&#39;s direction for a FaceContact, in assembled
    // world coordinates. Zero elsewhere.
    Direction r3.Vec
    // Pull is the direction in which A leaves B in an exploded view, in assembled
    // world coordinates, or zero. On a PinInBore or PinInSlot it picks the sense
    // along the axis; on any other kind it is the direction. Its length does not
    // matter.
    Pull r3.Vec
}</pre>

Joint connects part A to part B. A is the inserted or moving member (the pin,
the slider), B the receiver.

    // Separation is the distance between the two parts&#39; exploded boxes, zero
    // when they meet.
    Separation units.Value
}</pre>

Leader is the dotted line one joint draws in the exploded view.

<a name="Material"></a>
### type Material

<pre>type Material struct {
    Name    <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#string">string</a>
    Density units.Value
}</pre>

Material names what a part is made of. Name is a free label ("PETG",
"steel"). Density is a units.Density, or the zero Value when unknown; the
bill of materials then omits the mass.

<a name="Motion"></a>
### type Motion

<pre>type Motion <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int">int</a></pre>

Motion is what the joint lets A do against B. Fixed is the zero value.

<a name="Fixed"></a><a name="Turns"></a><a name="Slides"></a><a name="TurnsAndSlides"></a>

<pre>const (
    Fixed          <a href="#Motion">Motion</a> = iota
    Turns                 // about the joint axis
    Slides                // along Joint.Direction, or along a slot
    TurnsAndSlides        // about and along the joint axis
)</pre>

<a name="Motion.String"></a>
#### func (Motion) String

<pre>func (m <a href="#Motion">Motion</a>) String() <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#string">string</a></pre>

String returns the lower-case words for the motion.

<a name="Node"></a>
### type Node

<pre>type Node struct {
    Part, Group <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#string">string</a>
    Kind        <a href="#Kind">Kind</a>
}</pre>

Node is one part of the diagram.

<a name="Occlusion"></a>
### type Occlusion

<pre>type Occlusion struct {
    Front, Back <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#string">string</a>
    Covered     units.Value // Dimensionless: the share of Back&#39;s projected box that Front&#39;s covers
}</pre>

Occlusion says that one part may hide another seen along a view direction.

<a name="PairFinding"></a>
### type PairFinding

<pre>type PairFinding struct {
    A, B     <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#string">string</a>
    Overlap  decad.<a href="decad.md#Box">Box</a>              // where the two boxes, grown by the contact tolerance and their bounds, meet
    Near     *decad.<a href="decad.md#Measurement">Measurement</a>     // WithWitnessSearch: a proven gap upper bound at most the contact tolerance
    Verified *decad.<a href="decad.md#ContactRelation">ContactRelation</a> // the pair&#39;s relation in a WithVerifyReport report; nil without one
}</pre>

PairFinding is a pair of parts whose boxes meet and that no joint names.

<a name="Part"></a>
### type Part

<pre>type Part struct {
    // Name is unique within its Set and non-empty.
    Name <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#string">string</a>
    Kind <a href="#Kind">Kind</a>
    // Body is the part as placed in the assembled pose. A Manufactured part
    // MUST have one; a Purchased part may (a modeled band) or may not (a screw
    // that is only listed). Every body of a Set belongs to one document.
    Body     *decad.<a href="decad.md#Body">Body</a>
    Material <a href="#Material">Material</a>
    // Quantity is how many of a body-less part the build needs. A part with a
    // Body is one piece; its Quantity MUST be 0 or 1.
    Quantity <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int">int</a>
    // Spec groups identical parts in the bill of materials (&#34;pin 4 x 60&#34;,
    // &#34;rubber band 2 x 60&#34;). Parts sharing a non-empty Spec are one row.
    Spec <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#string">string</a>
}</pre>

Part is one piece of the build.

<a name="PartMesh"></a>
### type PartMesh

<pre>type PartMesh struct {
    Part      <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#string">string</a>
    Tolerance units.Value // the chord tolerance the part was read at
    Bound     units.Value // that mesh&#39;s bound
    Verified  <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#bool">bool</a>        // the mesh was built at VerifyAll
}</pre>

PartMesh says how one part's faces were read.

<a name="PartView"></a>
### type PartView

    Part      <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#string">string</a>
    Placement r3.Transform // assembled coordinates to view coordinates
    Bounds    decad.<a href="decad.md#Box">Box</a>    // the body&#39;s box in view coordinates
    Anchor    r3.Vec       // label anchor: the top centre of Bounds
    Ports     []<a href="#Port">Port</a>       // where each joint attaches, in view coordinates
}</pre>

PartView is one part posed for drawing.

<a name="PathState"></a>
### type PathState

<pre>type PathState <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int">int</a></pre>

PathState says what a part's straight path met, judged by boxes alone.

<a name="PathNone"></a><a name="PathClear"></a><a name="PathBlocked"></a><a name="PathEnclosed"></a><a name="PathStuck"></a>

<pre>const (
    PathNone     <a href="#PathState">PathState</a> = iota // the part did not move
    PathClear                     // its swept box meets no part it is not joined to
    PathBlocked                   // it starts clear and its sweep meets a part
    PathEnclosed                  // its start box already meets a part&#39;s box, so a box test cannot decide
    PathStuck                     // no distance clears it
)</pre>

<a name="PathState.String"></a>

<pre>func (p <a href="#PathState">PathState</a>) String() <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#string">string</a></pre>

<a name="Port"></a>
### type Port

<pre>type Port struct {
    Joint <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#string">string</a>
    Other <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#string">string</a> // the part at the joint&#39;s other end
    Point r3.Vec // the middle of the engagement, or the contact face&#39;s centre, or a box fallback
    Dir   r3.Vec // the axis or the face&#39;s outward normal; zero when none is known
}</pre>

Port is where one joint attaches to a part.

<a name="PullSource"></a>
### type PullSource

<pre>type PullSource <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int">int</a></pre>

PullSource says where the direction a part was pulled in came from.

<a name="PullNone"></a><a name="AxisFromFaces"></a><a name="AxisDeclared"></a><a name="FaceNormal"></a><a name="BoxCentres"></a><a name="PullDeclared"></a><a name="StageDirection"></a>

<pre>const (
    PullNone       <a href="#PullSource">PullSource</a> = iota // the ground, or a part no joint reaches
    AxisFromFaces                    // the axis of the matched cylinder faces
    AxisDeclared                     // the joint&#39;s declared Axis
    FaceNormal                       // the normal of the matched contact faces
    BoxCentres                       // the line between the two parts&#39; box centres
    PullDeclared                     // the joint&#39;s declared Pull

)</pre>

<pre>func (p <a href="#PullSource">PullSource</a>) String() <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#string">string</a></pre>

<a name="Removal"></a>
### type Removal

Removal constrains how WithDerivedExplode removes one part.

<pre>type Removal struct {
    // Direction, when not zero, is the only direction the part may leave by. Its
    // length does not matter.
    Direction r3.Vec
    // After names parts that must leave in an earlier round than this part.
    After []<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#string">string</a>
    // Before names parts this part must leave before.
    Before []<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#string">string</a>
    // Group puts every part with the same non-empty Group into one rigid group
    // that leaves together along one direction.
    Group <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#string">string</a>
}</pre>

<a name="Set"></a>
### type Set

<pre>type Set struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}</pre>

Set is the parts of one build and the joints between them. It is a builder:
its methods edit the Set, never the document. A Set is not safe for
concurrent mutation; queries may run concurrently while nothing mutates it.

<a name="NewSet"></a>
#### func NewSet

<pre>func NewSet(doc *decad.<a href="decad.md#Document">Document</a>) *<a href="#Set">Set</a></pre>

NewSet returns an empty [Set](<#Set>) over doc. doc MUST NOT be nil.

<a name="Set.Add"></a>
#### func (\*Set) Add

<pre>func (s *<a href="#Set">Set</a>) Add(p <a href="#Part">Part</a>) <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a></pre>

Add appends p. It refuses, with decad.ErrDegenerate, an empty or repeated
name, KindUnset, a Manufactured part without a body, a sheet body, a body
already in the [Set](<#Set>) and a Quantity outside its rule. A body of another
document is decad.ErrForeignBody.

<a name="Set.BOM"></a>
#### func (\*Set) BOM

<pre>func (s *<a href="#Set">Set</a>) BOM(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>) (*<a href="#BOM">BOM</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

[BOM](<#BOM>) returns the bill of materials. Parts sharing a Spec are one row; they must
agree: the same [Kind](<#Kind>) and material name, and volumes that overlap within their
bounds, or [BOM](<#BOM>) returns decad.ErrDegenerate naming the two parts. That check
only falsifies the caller's claim that the parts are the same. A part with a
body counts one; a body-less part counts its Quantity. Mass is the solid
body's mass: infill lowers it.

<a name="Set.Check"></a>
#### func (\*Set) Check

<pre>func (s *<a href="#Set">Set</a>) Check(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, opts ...<a href="#CheckOption">CheckOption</a>) (*<a href="#JointReport">JointReport</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

Check judges every declared joint against the faces and bounds of its two
parts, and lists the pairs of parts whose boxes meet with no joint naming
them (agent-docs/parts-design.md §7.2). It is a structural check: it never
calls Document.Verify, and it does not prove that two parts' interiors are
disjoint. A Contradicted joint is a finding, not an error.

Contact and Keepout joints are read from box gaps and point witnesses; a Tie is
NotChecked. A report from a Verify the caller already ran can settle what the
structural rules leave open (WithVerifyReport).

<a name="Set.Document"></a>
#### func (\*Set) Document

<pre>func (s *<a href="#Set">Set</a>) Document() *decad.<a href="decad.md#Document">Document</a></pre>

Document returns the document the [Set](<#Set>)'s bodies belong to.

<a name="Set.Explode"></a>
#### func (\*Set) Explode

<pre>func (s *<a href="#Set">Set</a>) Explode(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, opts ...<a href="#ExplodeOption">ExplodeOption</a>) (*<a href="#Exploded">Exploded</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

Explode places every part along its joints for an exploded view. It reads the
joints' axes from the faces and needs no Check. The joint graph is walked
breadth-first from the ground, joints in Join order, so each part has one
parent joint; a part reached twice keeps its first parent. Parts no joint
reaches keep a zero offset and Depth -1. Each part moves along its parent
joint's direction, in the sense whose swept box along the travel is strictly
disjoint from every other part's box except those joined to it, else the
shorter travel, then the sense with a positive largest component; the offset
is the travel that clears the parent plus WithExplodeGap.

WithExplodeStages runs that in ordered stages, WithPartGap and
WithExplodeScale tune the distances, and [Joint](<#Joint>).Pull states a direction
(agent-docs/parts-design.md §5.3).

<a name="Set.Graph"></a>
#### func (\*Set) Graph

<pre>func (s *<a href="#Set">Set</a>) Graph(r *<a href="#JointReport">JointReport</a>) <a href="#Graph">Graph</a></pre>

[Graph](<#Graph>) returns the connection diagram of the [Set](<#Set>). r may be nil; with one, each
edge carries its joint's status. A part whose body a later modelling step
retired has an empty Group.

<a name="Set.Group"></a>
#### func (\*Set) Group

<pre>func (s *<a href="#Set">Set</a>) Group(name <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#string">string</a>) (<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#string">string</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

Group returns the container path of the named part's body, joined with "/",
or "" for the root container and for a body-less part. A body consumed by a
later modelling step is decad.ErrRetiredBody.

<a name="Set.Infer"></a>
#### func (\*Set) Infer

<pre>func (s *<a href="#Set">Set</a>) Infer(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, opts ...<a href="#CheckOption">CheckOption</a>) ([]<a href="#InferredJoint">InferredJoint</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

Infer lists the pin-in-bore and pin-in-slot joints the faces suggest between
the parts (agent-docs/parts-design.md §7.3). For every pair of parts with
bodies whose boxes, grown by MaxFit, meet, it runs the matching of §7.1 in both
directions and returns each match, longest engagement first within a pair,
with the clearance it measured. A match is a convex cylinder face of one part
in a coaxial concave one of the other, or between two parallel planar faces; a
face that reads as neither a plane nor a cylinder never matches. [Joint](<#Joint>) names
are "A\~B", with "#2", "#3" for further matches of one pair. Infer adds nothing
to the [Set](<#Set>). Coplanar face contacts are not inferred.

<a name="Set.Join"></a>
#### func (\*Set) Join

<pre>func (s *<a href="#Set">Set</a>) Join(j <a href="#Joint">Joint</a>) <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a></pre>

Join appends j. It refuses, with decad.ErrDegenerate, an unknown part,
A == B, JointUnset, a repeated name, a Keepout without a positive MinGap, a
[Motion](<#Motion>) the kind cannot have, an [Axis](<#Axis>) on a kind without one or with a zero
direction, and a geometric kind naming a body-less part. A quantity of the
wrong kind is decad.ErrUnitKind and a non-finite one decad.ErrNotFinite. Join
normalises [Axis](<#Axis>).Dir.

<a name="Set.Joints"></a>
#### func (\*Set) Joints

<pre>func (s *<a href="#Set">Set</a>) Joints() []<a href="#Joint">Joint</a></pre>

Joints returns the joints in Join order.

<a name="Set.Linkage"></a>
#### func (\*Set) Linkage

<pre>func (s *<a href="#Set">Set</a>) Linkage(ground <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#string">string</a>, r *<a href="#JointReport">JointReport</a>) (*decad.<a href="decad.md#Linkage">Linkage</a>, []<a href="#Joint">Joint</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

Linkage builds a [decad.Linkage](<decad.md#Linkage>) from the [Set](<#Set>) (agent-docs/parts-design.md §7.4)
rooted at the ground part, and returns the joints it could not place.

Parts joined by Fixed pin, slot and face joints form one link; the ground's
link is the linkage's ground, whose bodies belong to no link and so stay
static. Walking the other joints breadth-first from the ground in Join order, a
Turns joint becomes a revolute about its axis, and a Slides joint a prismatic
along the joint's axis (a pin in a bore), along the slot (a pin in a slot) or
along Direction (a face contact). The axis comes from r, a report of Check, and
otherwise from the joint's declared [Axis](<#Axis>). Every Contact and Tie joint between
bodies of different links is declared a joint contact, as is each placed
pin, slot and face joint; a Keepout is not, since its parts must stay apart.

A joint is returned unplaced, for the caller's Linkage.Close or for repair,
when it would close a loop, when neither r nor the joint gives the axis or
slot direction it needs, or when it is a TurnsAndSlides joint: a cylindrical
joint is a revolute and a prismatic with an intermediate link that carries a
body, which a part joint cannot supply. r may be nil. A body-less part takes
no part. A part no placed joint reaches belongs to no link and is static.

<a name="Set.Part"></a>
#### func (\*Set) Part

<pre>func (s *<a href="#Set">Set</a>) Part(name <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#string">string</a>) (<a href="#Part">Part</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

[Part](<#Part>) returns the named part, or decad.ErrDegenerate for an unknown name.

<a name="Set.Parts"></a>
#### func (\*Set) Parts

<pre>func (s *<a href="#Set">Set</a>) Parts() []<a href="#Part">Part</a></pre>

Parts returns the parts in Add order.

<a name="Set.Views"></a>
#### func (\*Set) Views

<pre>func (s *<a href="#Set">Set</a>) Views(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, opts ...<a href="#ViewOption">ViewOption</a>) (*<a href="#Views">Views</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

[Views](<#Views>) returns the pose and joint ports of each part that has a body. A part
is posed by the translation that puts its box centre at the origin, keeping
the assembled orientation, or by its WithPartPose transform. The pose is for
drawing, not for making: [Views](<#Views>) offers no "lay it flat" frame, because
choosing the side a part rests on is a process decision.

A port's Point is the middle of the matched or declared axis over the
engagement, or the centre of the contact face for a FaceContact, or else the
centre of the two parts' box overlap (the midpoint of the shortest segment
between their boxes when they do not overlap), or the part's own box centre
when the other part has no body. Dir is the axis, or the part's own face
normal for a FaceContact; it is zero for the box fallback.

<a name="Stage"></a>
### type Stage

<pre>type Stage struct {
    Name   <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#string">string</a>   // non-empty and unique
    Parts  []<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#string">string</a> // part names
    Groups []<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#string">string</a> // container paths (Set.Group); every part in one, or below it, is a member
    // Gap is how far past clearing each member moves; the zero Value means
    // WithExplodeGap&#39;s gap.
    Gap units.Value
    // Clear says what the members must clear: ClearJoined (the zero value) or
    // ClearAll.
    Clear <a href="#Clearing">Clearing</a>
    // Direction, when not zero, moves every member along it instead of along its
    // joint (Pull then reads StageDirection). Its length does not matter.
    Direction r3.Vec
    // Together moves the members as one rigid group by one offset.
    Together <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#bool">bool</a>
}</pre>

Stage is one step of a staged explosion. Its parts move in it, in the order of
the joint walk; every other part stays where earlier stages left it.

<a name="Summary"></a>
### type Summary

<pre>type Summary struct {
    Set      *<a href="#Set">Set</a>
    Joints   *<a href="#JointReport">JointReport</a>
    Exploded *<a href="#Exploded">Exploded</a>
}</pre>

Summary is the agent-readable text form of the outputs. Every field but [Set](<#Set>)
is optional. It has no extension hook: a caller who wants its own sections on
the page writes them to the same [io.Writer](<https://pkg.go.dev/io#Writer>) after WriteMarkdown.

<a name="Summary.WriteMarkdown"></a>
#### func (Summary) WriteMarkdown

<pre>func (s <a href="#Summary">Summary</a>) WriteMarkdown(w io.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/io#Writer">Writer</a>) <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a></pre>

WriteMarkdown writes one page, in this order: the bill of materials table; the
joint table with each joint's status, cause and evidence, and the unexplained
pairs, when Joints is set; the exploded depth
and pull table when [Exploded](<#Exploded>) is set; the Mermaid connection diagram. Numbers
print with their bounds. A [Set](<#Set>) with a retired body is decad.ErrRetiredBody
and a nil [Set](<#Set>) decad.ErrDegenerate.

<a name="ViewOption"></a>
### type ViewOption

<pre>type ViewOption interface {
    // contains filtered or unexported methods
}</pre>

ViewOption configures [Views](<#Views>). The tolerance options of [CheckOption](<#CheckOption>) are
accepted too.

<a name="WithPartPose"></a>
#### func WithPartPose

<pre>func WithPartPose(part <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#string">string</a>, t r3.Transform) <a href="#ViewOption">ViewOption</a></pre>

WithPartPose makes [Views](<#Views>) pose the named part by t instead of centring it. t
maps assembled coordinates to view coordinates and must be a proper rigid
motion: a reflection or the zero Transform is decad.ErrDegenerate. A name no
part has is decad.ErrDegenerate at the query.

<a name="Views"></a>
### type Views

<pre>type Views struct{ Parts []<a href="#PartView">PartView</a> } // in Set order, body-less parts omitted
</pre>

Views is what a renderer needs to draw each part alone on a part sheet.
